accounting.interpretation: Guest aggregate ticks undercount process accounting in some windows. Aggregate added percentages are noisy screens, not calibrated CPU budgets. CPU and kernel-reported BPF runtime must not be summed; BPF snapshots include extra observer time.

rejected_attempts.reason: bpftool presentation lacked required timing counters; switched to exact kernel info API.

Two timing attempts and a diagnostic run rejected raw module snapshot changes. Diagnostic identified inet_diag references3-to2 with unchanged identity. Final audit compares identities and retains raw reference changes separately; BPF program ID-set audit unchanged.

limitations: QEMU guest on a non-Intel host; physical Intel required before claiming fleet CPU percentages.
Three repeats per condition, short windows, timing quantization and background noise; retain ranges and negative deltas.
Whole-guest/app CPU windows include application startup and equal0.5s settling; the write-loop-only figure is a separate incomplete accounting view.
Excluded-Python control uses an intentionally unobservable cgroup ID through the direct collector; it is not a deployable service configuration.
Python metadata remains unattested. Fixture identity/source checks do not prove general coverage or arbitrary missed-callback correctness.
No production CPU optimization shipped in this measurement batch.
recommendation: First address global Python probes with explicit source scope and lifecycle/cross-boundary regression controls. Native opening-state copies are the next measured BPF target. Keep identity-only default; do not remove return binding or add stack caches without correctness proof.
